body.heading: Remember being new
paragraphs: Everyone has stood in a doorway calculating whether they belong. The new colleague, the new neighbour, the friend-of-a-friend at the party: their hesitation is not aloofness, it is arithmetic — and your invitation changes the sums completely.
It takes so little because the alternative they are comparing it with is standing alone.

body.heading: Absorb the small risks
paragraphs: Yes, the invitation might be declined, or the new person might be quiet at first, or the group might need a week to warm. These are tiny risks, and they are yours to absorb — that absorption is precisely the generosity involved.
Introduce them properly when they come: name, one kind fact, one shared thread. A good introduction is a bridge built in ten seconds.

body.heading: It changes the group too
paragraphs: Groups that regularly absorb newcomers stay alive; groups sealed shut slowly become museums of their own history. The new person brings new stories, new skills, and the useful reminder that the world is bigger than the current membership.
One day the new person will be you again. The culture of invitation you help build is the one that will catch you.

takeaway: Absorb the tiny risk, introduce them well, and let the group grow by one.
